tools.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
tools.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp
tools.description: Close a tab in the MCP tab group by its ID. Use to clean up tabs you're done with. Only tabs in this session's group are closable; call tabs_context_mcp first to get valid IDs. If you close the group's last tab, Chrome auto-removes the group — the next tabs_context_mcp with createIfEmpty starts fresh.

tabId.description: The ID of the tab to close. Must be in this session's tab group. Get valid IDs from tabs_context_mcp.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
tools.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
tools.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

Title: INSURANCE-01 Class Code and Premium Audit Assistant
URL: https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/mobilebasic
Source element: <body>
---
INSURANCE-01 Class Code and Premium Audit Assistant
Class Code and Premium Audit Assistant
Scenario

Linden Shore Mutual writes workers' compensation insurance in Maryland. Underwriting is quoting six new employers, and before a quote goes out the premium audit team checks that each employer's payroll sits under the right class code. Employers fill in their own payroll split on the application, and the audit team confirms or corrects it from the employer's records. Nadia Brennan, Senior Premium Auditor, wants a reusable Agent Skill that does the first pass on any employer file: suggest the class codes, allocate the payroll to them, and list the questions she should put to the employer. The company, people, employers and records are fictional.

Your task

Interview Nadia Brennan to learn how her team classifies people and counts payroll, and where the employer files and the company's classification rules are kept. Then build the Skill and run it on all six employers: Harbor Point Legal, Bay Crest Exteriors, Severn Homebuilders, Patuxent Electric, Annapolis Courier and Larkspur Lane Bistro.

The employer files and the classification rules are not in the starter repository. Read them from the locations the auditor gives you, during each run. This company uses its own class codes; public classification manuals do not apply and will give wrong answers. Where the written rules leave a case open, or an employer's records disagree with what the employer reported, find out from the auditor how her team handles it rather than guessing, and say in the report which records decided each case. The Skill classifies and allocates payroll only; it does not set rates or quote premium.

Deliverables

Interview records: interviews/*.md. Include the original Markdown export of every interview session, with its session metadata and complete participant-visible messages. Keep one final complete export per session without rewriting or summarizing it, and commit it with your code. If the export is unavailable, contact the facilitator; do not manufacture a replacement.

Paths are relative to your repository.

Path

Required content

skills/class-code-assistant/SKILL.md

Reusable Skill instructions with name and description metadata, inputs, invocation, outputs, error behavior and references to its supporting files

Supporting Skill files

Your code and focused references under the Skill or documented project paths; no answers hard-coded for these six employers

README.md

Setup, the command that runs the Skill on one employer and on all six, and how you verified the results

deliverables/codes/<employer>.csv

One file per employer, named harbor-point-legal.csv, bay-crest-exteriors.csv, severn-homebuilders.csv, patuxent-electric.csv, annapolis-courier.csv and larkspur-lane-bistro.csv. Columns exactly class_code,payroll_allocated,rationale_ref: one row per class code that carries payroll at that employer for the audit period, no rows with zero payroll. payroll_allocated is US dollars to the cent without thousands separators. rationale_ref is the identifier, exactly as printed in the company's classification rules, of the paragraph that describes the code

deliverables/audit-questions.md

One section per employer with the questions the auditor should put to the employer before signing off. Each question names the employee, subcontractor or record it is about. Every adjustment you make, and every record your decision relies on, has at least one question asking the employer to confirm it

deliverables/audit-report.md

One section per employer: the codes and payroll you allocated; where and why your allocation differs from the employer's own split; every adjustment, naming the employee or payment it concerns and its amount to the cent; and the records that support it

Coding-session evidence

The capture tool's real session records for the submitted code revision; self-written logs do not substitute for them

In your coding session, decide and state in your own words whether you accept each employer's own payroll split, and what record that decision rests on.

Interview

Interview Nadia Brennan, Senior Premium Auditor, through the interview channel the facilitator provides. Investigate the business work and obtain the rules, source locations and explanations you need; no special question wording is required.

This is a real-case Challenge, closer to client work. The course rule is to plan for at most 3 conversations with the stakeholder, so prepare before each conversation and ask completely.

Interview rule. You conduct the stakeholder interview yourself, and the questions are yours. Do not connect a coding agent or any other AI to the interview to run, script, or automate it. The interview transcript is assessed together with the code; a project whose interview was run by an agent is not scored.

Submit

Commit the Skill, the deliverables and interviews/ to your repository and keep your coding session captured. Keep secrets out of the repository. Your README must explain how to rerun the Skill on a new employer file.

---
INSURANCE-01 Class Code and Premium Audit Assistant
Class Code and Premium Audit Assistant
Scenario

Linden Shore Mutual writes workers' compensation insurance in Maryland. Underwriting is quoting six new employers, and before a quote goes out the premium audit team checks that each employer's payroll sits under the right class code. Employers fill in their own payroll split on the application, and the audit team confirms or corrects it from the employer's records. Nadia Brennan, Senior Premium Auditor, wants a reusable Agent Skill that does the first pass on any employer file: suggest the class codes, allocate the payroll to them, and list the questions she should put to the employer. The company, people, employers and records are fictional.

Your task

Interview Nadia Brennan to learn how her team classifies people and counts payroll, and where the employer files and the company's classification rules are kept. Then build the Skill and run it on all six employers: Harbor Point Legal, Bay Crest Exteriors, Severn Homebuilders, Patuxent Electric, Annapolis Courier and Larkspur Lane Bistro.

The employer files and the classification rules are not in the starter repository. Read them from the locations the auditor gives you, during each run. This company uses its own class codes; public classification manuals do not apply and will give wrong answers. Where the written rules leave a case open, or an employer's records disagree with what the employer reported, find out from the auditor how her team handles it rather than guessing, and say in the report which records decided each case. The Skill classifies and allocates payroll only; it does not set rates or quote premium.

Deliverables

Interview records: interviews/*.md. Include the original Markdown export of every interview session, with its session metadata and complete participant-visible messages. Keep one final complete export per session without rewriting or summarizing it, and commit it with your code. If the export is unavailable, contact the facilitator; do not manufacture a replacement.

Paths are relative to your repository.

Path

Required content

skills/class-code-assistant/SKILL.md

Reusable Skill instructions with name and description metadata, inputs, invocation, outputs, error behavior and references to its supporting files

Supporting Skill files

Your code and focused references under the Skill or documented project paths; no answers hard-coded for these six employers

README.md

Setup, the command that runs the Skill on one employer and on all six, and how you verified the results

deliverables/codes/<employer>.csv

One file per employer, named harbor-point-legal.csv, bay-crest-exteriors.csv, severn-homebuilders.csv, patuxent-electric.csv, annapolis-courier.csv and larkspur-lane-bistro.csv. Columns exactly class_code,payroll_allocated,rationale_ref: one row per class code that carries payroll at that employer for the audit period, no rows with zero payroll. payroll_allocated is US dollars to the cent without thousands separators. rationale_ref is the identifier, exactly as printed in the company's classification rules, of the paragraph that describes the code

deliverables/audit-questions.md

One section per employer with the questions the auditor should put to the employer before signing off. Each question names the employee, subcontractor or record it is about. Every adjustment you make, and every record your decision relies on, has at least one question asking the employer to confirm it

deliverables/audit-report.md

One section per employer: the codes and payroll you allocated; where and why your allocation differs from the employer's own split; every adjustment, naming the employee or payment it concerns and its amount to the cent; and the records that support it

Coding-session evidence

The capture tool's real session records for the submitted code revision; self-written logs do not substitute for them

In your coding session, decide and state in your own words whether you accept each employer's own payroll split, and what record that decision rests on.

Interview

Interview Nadia Brennan, Senior Premium Auditor, through the interview channel the facilitator provides. Investigate the business work and obtain the rules, source locations and explanations you need; no special question wording is required.

This is a real-case Challenge, closer to client work. The course rule is to plan for at most 3 conversations with the stakeholder, so prepare before each conversation and ask completely.

Interview rule. You conduct the stakeholder interview yourself, and the questions are yours. Do not connect a coding agent or any other AI to the interview to run, script, or automate it. The interview transcript is assessed together with the code; a project whose interview was run by an agent is not scored.

Submit

Commit the Skill, the deliverables and interviews/ to your repository and keep your coding session captured. Keep secrets out of the repository. Your README must explain how to rerun the Skill on a new employer file.

16:38
Do this before your first class. In class we check it is done; we do not do it together.

entire.io records how you work with your agent. Those records are one of the three things your work is assessed on, and they cannot be recreated later, so set this up before any real work, in every project copy.

Ask your agent to set it up

In ChatGPT, open a Codex conversation in your financial-health-brief folder, paste this and send it:

Install the entire.io command-line tool if it is not installed. Then enable it in this repository for Codex with entire enable -y --agent codex, and show me the output of entire status.

If you work in Claude Code or OpenCode instead, write claude-code or opencode where it says codex. Choosing the wrong agent looks like it worked and records nothing.

Your agent may refuse to run the installer, because it downloads a script and runs it. If it hands you the command, paste it into your terminal yourself, as "Install your coding agent" describes.

Every time you hand in

Ask your agent to commit your work, show you that entire checkpoint list recorded it, and push. If the push needs you to sign in to GitHub, the agent will hand that step to you.

Hand in by submitting your copy's GitHub link in the project's assignment. Never commit passwords, API keys or other secrets.

You are done when

Your agent has shown you entire status saying entire.io is enabled in financial-health-brief.

# ch03 INSURANCE-01 materials notes (read 2026-10-23)

Sources read: Classroom assignment page, assignment Google Doc (1Du534hc...), Classroom material "4. Recording your sessions with entire.io".
Not opened: stakeholder interview link (work-sim.catalyte.ai/s/ch03-premium-audit), Kuan runs it herself.

## Scope
- Linden Shore Mutual, workers' comp, Maryland. Fictional.
- Skill does first pass on ANY employer file: suggest class codes, allocate payroll, list questions for employer.
- Does NOT set rates or quote premium.
- Six employers: Harbor Point Legal, Bay Crest Exteriors, Severn Homebuilders, Patuxent Electric, Annapolis Courier, Larkspur Lane Bistro.
- Employers self-report payroll split; audit team confirms/corrects from employer records.
- Employer files + classification rules NOT in repo; ask Nadia where; read from there DURING EACH RUN.
- Company uses its own class codes; public manuals (NCCI etc.) give wrong answers.
- Where rules leave a case open, or records disagree with employer's report: ask Nadia how her team handles it, do not guess; report says which records decided each case.

## Deliverables
- interviews/*.md: original Markdown export per session, with session metadata + complete participant-visible messages. One final complete export per session, no rewriting. If export unavailable, contact facilitator.
- skills/class-code-assistant/SKILL.md: name + description metadata, inputs, invocation, outputs, error behavior, refs to supporting files.
- Supporting files: code + focused references; NO answers hard-coded for the six.
- README.md: setup, command for one employer and all six, how verified, how to rerun on a new employer file. Keep Interview rule.
- deliverables/codes/<slug>.csv, six files: harbor-point-legal, bay-crest-exteriors, severn-homebuilders, patuxent-electric, annapolis-courier, larkspur-lane-bistro.
  - Columns exactly: class_code,payroll_allocated,rationale_ref
  - One row per code carrying payroll in audit period; no zero rows.
  - payroll_allocated: USD to the cent, no thousands separators.
  - rationale_ref: paragraph identifier exactly as printed in company rules.
- deliverables/audit-questions.md: section per employer; each question names the employee/subcontractor/record; every adjustment and every relied-on record has >=1 confirming question.
- deliverables/audit-report.md: section per employer: codes + payroll; where/why differs from employer's split; every adjustment naming employee/payment + amount to the cent; supporting records.
- Coding-session evidence: entire.io real records for submitted revision.
- In the coding session Kuan must state IN HER OWN WORDS whether she accepts each employer's own split and what record it rests on.

## Interview
- Max 3 conversations planned; prepare, ask completely.
- Kuan conducts it herself; questions are hers; no AI connected to run/script/automate.

## Capture (entire.io)
- Enable with the correct agent (claude-code here). Verified: entire status shows Agents · Claude Code.
- Each hand-in: commit, show entire checkpoint list recorded it, push.
- Never commit secrets.

## Open / unclear
- Classroom "Submit" says follow assignment for "access information", but the doc says nothing about repo access (public vs private, collaborator). Ask facilitator.
- Starter repo is GitRollTraining/ch03-premium-audit; Kuan's working copy is kuanrur/ch03-premium-audit.
- Classwork "Set up your environment" items 1 to 3 not read.

教材讀完了，可以開始。我讀了三份：Classroom 的 assignment 頁、assignment Google Doc，還有「4. Recording your sessions with entire.io」那頁。Stakeholder interview 的連結我沒有打開。

**capture 這邊已經符合要求**
那頁特別提醒，agent 選錯會「looks like it worked and records nothing」。之前 `entire status` 顯示的是 `Agents · Claude Code`，選對了。每次交作業要做三件事：commit、用 `entire checkpoint list` 確認有記錄、push。剛才那次三件都做了。

**任務的核心**
- Linden Shore Mutual 的 workers' comp 業務，地點在 Maryland，公司和人物都是虛構的。要做一個 Skill，拿到任何一家 employer 的檔案都能做第一輪處理：建議 class code、把 payroll 分配到各個 code、列出要問 employer 的問題。這個 Skill 不定費率，也不報保費。
- 員工資料檔和分類規則都不在 repo 裡，要問 Nadia 放在哪裡，而且每次執行時都要從那裡讀。
- 這家公司用自己的 class code，公開的分類手冊（例如 NCCI）在這裡會給出錯誤答案。
- 規則沒寫到的情況，或是 employer 的紀錄和他們自己申報的對不上時，要問 Nadia 她的團隊怎麼處理，不能用猜的。報告裡要寫出每個判斷是根據哪份紀錄。

**交付物裡最容易出錯的細節**
- CSV 的欄位名稱必須完全是 `class_code,payroll_allocated,rationale_ref`。金額要算到分，不能有千分位逗號，payroll 為零的 code 不要列。`rationale_ref` 要照規則文件裡印的段落編號一字不差地寫。
- 六個檔名都有規定，例如 `harbor-point-legal.csv`。
- `audit-questions.md` 裡每個問題都要點名是哪位員工、哪個 subcontractor 或哪份紀錄。每一個調整、每一份判斷時用到的紀錄，都至少要有一題請 employer 確認。
- `audit-report.md` 裡每個調整都要寫出人名或款項，以及精確到分的金額。
- 程式裡不能把這六家的答案寫死。
- 有一件事只能由妳來做：在 coding session 裡，**用妳自己的話**說出每一家 employer 自己申報的 payroll split 妳接不接受，以及根據的是哪份紀錄。這段會從 entire 的紀錄裡看。
- 訪談的 export 要放原始 Markdown，每個 session 一份，不能改寫。

**我讀到但不清楚的一點，供妳參考**
Classroom 的 Submit 寫著要照 assignment 提供「access information」，但 Google Doc 裡沒有任何關於 repo 存取權限的說明，例如要不要公開、要不要加 collaborator。這要問 facilitator。另外，Classwork 裡「Set up your environment」的第 1 到 3 項我沒有讀。

上次提到的界線我會照著做：妳讀完教材後講給我聽，我幫妳對照有沒有理解錯的地方。但訪談題目是妳的，我不會幫妳擬，也不會在訪談前幫妳改。

content.text:
這兩件事要先講清楚。

**1. 訪談清單沒有附上來**
妳的訊息裡只有文字，沒有清單，`interviews/` 裡也只有 `.gitkeep`。可以直接貼在對話裡，或告訴我檔案路徑。

Export 讀完了。檔案在 `~/Downloads/ch03-premium-audit-20261023-2158.md`，我沒有動它。

**這次拿到的資訊**
- **檔案位置**：employer 檔案在一個 Drive 資料夾 `drive.google.com/drive/folders/1pt8gzX8...`，分類規則是一個 Drive 檔案「Classification guide excerpt」`drive.google.com/file/d/1L5MxLny...`。兩個連結我都還沒有打開，打不打得開、是什麼格式都**未驗證**。
- **每家的文件**：business description、按人和職位列出的 payroll register、Nadia 的 field notes，還有從 employer 收來的 logs 和 timesheets。
- **怎麼分類**：依照員工實際做的工作，不看職稱。
- **申報和紀錄衝突時**：紀錄永遠優先，連 Nadia 自己記得的事都比不上紀錄。每一個調整都要列進問題清單，讓 employer 確認。
- **Subcontractor**：拿不出 certificate of insurance 的，付給他的金額按 60% 計入 employer 的 payroll，歸在他實際做的工作對應的 code 下。
- **誰看結果**：數字交給 Underwriting，問題清單直接寄給 employer 的 owner。
- **驗收**：payroll split 要和紀錄對得上，並且符合分類規則和「house practices」。所有未解決的項目都要先確認過，報告才能定案。
- **Audit period**：Nadia 不知道。
- **新需求，assignment 裡沒寫**：週五前她只來得及打電話給兩家 employer，要妳告訴她先打哪兩家，以及理由。

**和妳清單相比還沒問到或沒得到答案的**
- 「Team practice where the written rules leave a case open」這題沒有問到。Nadia 自己提到了「house practices」，但這些做法寫在哪裡、內容是什麼，都還不知道。
- 「What counts as payroll」沒有得到答案。她回的是分類的原則，沒說哪些錢算 payroll，例如加班費、獎金、小費、owner 的薪資。
- 「what form she wants them in」只得到「誰看」，沒有得到要什麼形式。
- 一個人同時做好幾種工作時，payroll 怎麼拆到不同的 code，這點也沒有談到。
- Subcontractor 的 60% 規則，是寫在 guide 裡還是只是她口頭說的，不清楚。

**妳要我抓的錯**
- 第 167 行問到 premium，超出這個任務的範圍，Nadia 也轉介給了 Priya Okafor。這題算是浪費掉了。
- 語音轉文字之後有幾句變形了，例如第 53 行「Where do play employer files...」、第 187 行。Nadia 都聽懂了，但看 transcript 的人會讀到這些句子。
- 妳的名字被轉成了「Quan」。

Export 裡有很多 Nadia 的訊息重複出現，有些還在句子中間被截斷，例如第 49、141、183 行。這是工具輸出的原貌，照規定不能修改。
